newsitem.title: UK: U.K. drivers warm to green vehicles with subsidies.
newsitem.headline: U.K. drivers warm to green vehicles with subsidies.

text.p: Britain's efforts to encourage the use of cleaner motor fuels have already paid dividends with offers of subsidies resulting in a 20 million stg order for green vehicles, the Energy Saving Trust said on Friday.
Bus companies, local authorities and other organisations on Friday put out to tender a bulk order for 318 vehicles which will be partly funded by the Trust's Powershift program.
The order is for a wide range of vehicles, including small cars, waste disposal trucks, ambulances, police cars and buses.
The vehicles will be powered by one of the three green fuels: electricity, natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

"This is good news for businesses, local authorities, manufacturers, people living in cities, sufferers of asthma and heart disease and, of course, the environment," said Jonathan Murray, Powershift's program manager.
Powershift is a three-year initiative to reduce greenhouse gas emissions run by the Energy Saving Trust, and funded by the Department of the Environment, Transport and the Regions.

It helps reduce costs of clean fuel vehicles by placing bulk orders for interested buyers and subsidising up to 50 percent of the difference between the cost of a green vehicle and its conventionally fuelled alternative.
By taking part in the scheme a bus operator could save up to 130,000 stg on an electric bus, 35,000 stg on an LPG bus and 40,000 stg on a natural gas bus.
British Gas Natural Gas Vehicles, a unit of Centrica, said Friday's order was the biggest single boost Britain's green vehicle market has seen.

"The Powershift scheme will stimulate a number of fleets powered by compressed natural gas. They will need refuelling and we'll be developing 'Gas Stations' for them," said Tom Gorman, head of British Gas NGV in a statement.
